root_cause.text: The mt76 remain-on-channel path in drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/channel.c incorrectly invoked the locking wrapper mt76_set_channel() from mt76_remain_on_channel() and mt76_roc_complete() while dev->mutex was already held, causing self-deadlock, and it also failed to stop mac_work before taking that mutex, allowing a workqueue-related deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that “mt76_remain_on_channel() and mt76_roc_complete() call mt76_set_channel() while already holding dev->mutex” and that “mt76_set_channel() also acquires dev->mutex, this results in a deadlock”; the patch replaces mt76_set_channel() with __mt76_set_channel() in both functions and adds cancel_delayed_work_sync(&phy->mac_work) before mutex_lock(&dev->mutex) “to prevent a secondary deadlock with the mac_work workqueue.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the internal channel-setting helper when restoring the main channel after ROC completion to fix incorrect behavior in this path.
intent_record.what: The call to mt76_set_channel(phy, &phy->main_chandef, false) in mt76_roc_complete() was replaced with __mt76_set_channel(phy, &phy->main_chandef, false), while keeping the surrounding condition and arguments otherwise unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, channel restoration after ROC completion now uses the lower-level internal channel-setting function instead of the wrapper, which changes the execution path for switching back to the main channel and likely avoids extra wrapper-side handling during this completion path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending PHY mac_work before remain-on-channel setup to avoid concurrent work interfering with ROC handling.
intent_record.what: A call to cancel_delayed_work_sync(&phy->mac_work) was added in mt76_remain_on_channel() immediately after validating that phy is non-NULL and before taking dev->mutex.
intent_record.how: This synchronously cancels any pending mac_work for the selected PHY before starting remain-on-channel handling, preventing that delayed worker from running concurrently or interfering with the upcoming ROC operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle remain-on-channel channel-switch failures by aborting setup and rolling back ROC state and link references.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct call to mt76_set_channel(phy, &chandef, true) with an assignment of the return value from __mt76_set_channel(phy, &chandef, true) to ret, and adds an error-handling block that, on nonzero ret, clears mlink->mvif->roc_phy, phy->roc_vif, and phy->roc_link, releases the vif/phy link with mt76_put_vif_phy_link(phy, vif, mlink), and jumps to out instead of continuing.
intent_record.how: At runtime, remain-on-channel setup now detects channel-switch failures and aborts the operation cleanly instead of always proceeding as if channel configuration succeeded. This prevents ieee80211_ready_on_channel and delayed ROC work from being scheduled after a failed channel set, while also rolling back previously stored ROC state and releasing the acquired link reference.

grouping_result.intent: Use the internal channel-setting helper when restoring the main channel after ROC completion to fix incorrect behavior in this path.
Handle remain-on-channel channel-switch failures by aborting setup and rolling back ROC state and link references.

consistency_review.core_intent: Make remain-on-channel setup robust by preventing concurrent PHY/mac work interference and rolling back ROC state cleanly when channel-switch setup fails.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets the ROC completion channel-restore path implicated in the bug, replacing the locking wrapper with the internal helper while the mutex is already held, which directly addresses the self-deadlock root cause.

The changes directly target the remain-on-channel deadlock root cause by stopping pending mac_work before ROC setup, which addresses the workqueue-related deadlock mechanism, and they modify ROC setup/rollback logic in the same failing path when channel-switch setup fails.

candidates.rationale: This calls the locking wrapper from mt76_roc_complete() while dev->mutex is already held, directly causing the self-deadlock described in the root cause.
This invokes mt76_set_channel() from mt76_remain_on_channel() after dev->mutex has already been taken, causing recursive locking/self-deadlock.
Taking dev->mutex before stopping pending mac_work enables the workqueue-related deadlock, since concurrent mac_work may need the same mutex and interfere with ROC handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is in mt76_remain_on_channel() and calls the locking wrapper mt76_set_channel() while dev->mutex is already held, directly causing the self-deadlock described in the root cause.

This statement is in mt76_roc_complete() and likewise invokes the locking wrapper mt76_set_channel() while dev->mutex is already held, causing the same recursive locking/self-deadlock in the ROC completion path.

In the remain-on-channel path, taking dev->mutex at this point before stopping pending mac_work allows a workqueue-related deadlock, because concurrent mac_work can contend on the same mutex during ROC handling.

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the complete remain-on-channel and ROC completion paths, including locking and channel switching. The vulnerable construct is present: `mt76_remain_on_channel()` takes `mutex_lock(&dev->mutex);` and then calls `mt76_set_channel(phy, &chandef, true);` while the mutex is held. Likewise, `mt76_roc_complete_work()` takes `mutex_lock(&dev->mutex);` and calls `mt76_roc_complete(phy);`, and inside `mt76_roc_complete()` the code calls `mt76_set_channel(phy, &phy->main_chandef, false);` when `phy->main_chandef.chan` is set. Per the root cause, `mt76_set_channel()` is the locking wrapper and must not be invoked while `dev->mutex` is already held, so this introduces the self-deadlock condition. The workqueue-related fix is also absent: there is no call to stop/cancel `mac_work` before taking `dev->mutex` in these ROC paths. `mt76_abort_roc()` only does `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&phy->roc_work);` before locking, which does not address the missing `mac_work` stop described in the root cause. Therefore this commit contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.
